title: Dodgers three-peat bid ends with NLCS sweep by Brewers
text:
Ohtani ends longest HR drought of his career with a 3-run shot in the second inning but Dodgers pitchers couldn’t hold off relentless Brewers in a 6-4 loss.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, center, makes a mound visit during the fifth inning of Game 4 of the National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers on Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026, at Dodger Stadium.
The Dodgers lost, 6-4, and saw their bid for a third straight World Series title end in a sweep. LOS ANGELES — In the end, it was all too much – coming back from an 0-3 deficit, winning a third consecutive World Series championship. Shohei Ohtani came back to life after two months of ugly at-bats, unfamiliar criticism and questions about whether he even belonged in the Dodgers’ lineup.
His three-run home run in the second inning Thursday night gave the Dodgers a four-run lead – unheard of in this postseason of run suppression. That wasn’t enough to keep their season alive against a relentless Milwaukee Brewers’ team that just kept coming, taking a 6-4 win in Game 4 Thursday night to complete a four-game sweep of the two-time defending champions and advance from the National League Championship Series to their first World Series in 44 years.
After falling behind on Garrett Mitchell’s home run off Tanner Scott in the sixth inning, the Dodgers put the tying run on third base with one out in the sixth, seventh and eighth innings but couldn’t move him another 90 feet. Their dreams of a three-peat were buried under another collection of failed at-bats with a runner in scoring position. They went 2 for 11 in those situations in Game 4, 5 for 43 in the postseason.
The New York Yankees of 1998-2000 are still the most recent team to ‘three-peat’ as World Series champions. A National League franchise still hasn’t done it. After losing Game 3 on Wednesday night to become the 42nd team in MLB history to fall behind 0-3 in a best-of-seven series, the Dodgers said all the right things about becoming just the second to climb out of that hole and win the series.
“Four one-game winning streaks,” Kike’ Hernandez said. “We’ve won four in a row a number of times this year, ten times, I think,” Dave Roberts said. With the Brewers rolling out a ‘bullpen game’ in Game 4, opener Shane Drohan was gone after a leadoff single by Kyle Tucker in the second inning.
Former Dodger Dustin May replaced him and gave up another single to Teoscar Hernandez, struck out Max Muncy then gave up an RBI single to Andy Pages – the only Dodger who seemed able to hit with a runner in scoring position this postseason. Kike’ Hernandez flew out, bringing Ohtani to the plate with two outs.
He struck out against Drohan in the first inning but had finished Game 3 with a 113.5 mph exit velocity on an eighth-inning single – the kind of hard contact missing from Ohtani since mid-August and one of the signs that convinced Roberts to move him back to leadoff for Game 4. May threw Ohtani a 1-and-1 cutter in at his knees and Ohtani crushed it.
It left his bat at 113.1 mph and traveled 428 feet into the right-field pavilion. The emotion that burst out of Ohtani was just as explosive. As the crowd roared, he bounced down the first-base line, screaming and gesturing at his teammates in the dugout. The Dodgers’ first home run in the NLCS ended the longest home-run drought of Ohtani’s career at 25 games and 116 plate appearances.
The only thing that seemed longer was how long the Dodgers were going to have to work to make that four-run second inning stand up. Starter Tyler Glasnow retired the first 10 Brewers in order and struck out six of the first eight. He didn’t have another strikeout. It was nothing but contact from the Brewers after that.
A walk and back-to-back ground-rule doubles – the second by Jake Bauers – cut the Dodgers’ lead in half. An inning later, Glasnow walked the No. 8 hitter, Sal Frelick, who stole second and scored on a single by the No. 9 hitter David Hamilton. Glasnow was replaced by Evan Phillips who walked three in a row to force in the tying run.
The four aces the Dodgers thought would give them the upper hand in this postseason did not. Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Glasnow combined for a 6.50 ERA in the series against the Brewers. Only Skubal allowed fewer than three runs in his start. Tanner Scott came on for the sixth inning.
He didn’t give up a home run to a left-handed batter all season. The Brewers’ first batter in the sixth, left-handed Garrett Mitchell, has just two home runs off left-handed pitchers in his 286 career regular-season games. Scott left a full-count fastball over the heart of the plate and Mitchell sent it over the center field wall for his second home run off a left-handed pitcher in three at-bats .
The Brewers’ bullpen took over from there. The Dodgers got Kyle Tucker to third base after his one-out double in the sixth, Pages to third after his leadoff double in the seventh and Will Smith to third when Brewers right fielder Sal Frelick fumbled his double in the right field corner. The six at-bats with a chance to push across the tying run ended in three strikeouts, two ground outs and a shallow pop up to center field.
Hamilton made it a two-run lead with a solo home run in the top of the ninth. It was just the fifth hit of the game for the Brewers.
